passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: A sacrament is a visible sign of invisible grace, instituted by Jesus Christ for our sanctification.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: St. Thomas defines a sacrament as an efficacious outward sign instituted by Christ to confer invisible sanctifying grace.
passages.fullText: 1. A sacrament is a visible sign of invisible grace, instituted by Jesus Christ for our sanctification.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: Just as the natural life of man requires birth, growth, nourishment, healing from disease, recovery of strength, social governance, and propagation, so the supernatural life of grace requires the seven Sacraments.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The seven sacraments correspond by divine design to the essential stages, needs, and preservation of human bodily and social life.
passages.fullText: 2. Just as the natural life of man requires birth, growth, nourishment, healing from disease, recovery of strength, social governance, and propagation, so the supernatural life of grace requires the seven Sacraments.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: The seven Sacraments of the New Law are: Baptism, Confirmation, the Holy Eucharist, Penance, Extreme Unction, Holy Orders, and Matrimony.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: St. Thomas provides the definitive list of the seven Sacraments established under the New Law.
passages.fullText: 3. The seven Sacraments of the New Law are: Baptism, Confirmation, the Holy Eucharist, Penance, Extreme Unction, Holy Orders, and Matrimony.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: Each sacrament consists of sensible matter (actions or elements) and sacred form (the words spoken by the minister), conferring grace through the power of Christ's Passion.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Sacraments are intrinsically constituted of sensible matter and sacred form, deriving their grace-conferring power from Christ's Passion.
passages.fullText: 4. Each sacrament consists of sensible matter (actions or elements) and sacred form (the words spoken by the minister), conferring grace through the power of Christ's Passion.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: Baptism is the sacrament of spiritual regeneration through water and the Word of God, as Christ commanded in Matthew 28:19: "Baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Baptism is defined as the sacrament of spiritual rebirth through water and the Word in obedience to Christ's Great Commission.
passages.fullText: 1. Baptism is the sacrament of spiritual regeneration through water and the Word of God, as Christ commanded in Matthew 28:19: "Baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: It cleanses the soul from original sin and all actual sins, remits all eternal and temporal punishment due to sin, and imprints an indelible spiritual character marking the recipient as a member of Christ.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Baptism entirely removes original and actual guilt, remits all due punishment, and imprints an indelible character incorporating the soul into Christ.
passages.fullText: 2. It cleanses the soul from original sin and all actual sins, remits all eternal and temporal punishment due to sin, and imprints an indelible spiritual character marking the recipient as a member of Christ.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: It infuses sanctifying grace, the theological virtues of faith, hope, and charity, and makes the baptized an adopted child of God and heir to the kingdom of heaven (John 3:5).
passages.oneSentenceSummary: By imparting sanctifying grace and the theological virtues, Baptism establishes divine filiation and makes the recipient an heir of heaven.
passages.fullText: 3. It infuses sanctifying grace, the theological virtues of faith, hope, and charity, and makes the baptized an adopted child of God and heir to the kingdom of heaven (John 3:5).

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: The ordinary minister of Baptism is a bishop, priest, or deacon, but in case of necessity any person using true water and the Trinitarian form can validly baptize.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: While ordained ministers are the ordinary ministers of Baptism, necessity permits anyone to validly baptize with water and the Trinitarian form.
passages.fullText: 4. The ordinary minister of Baptism is a bishop, priest, or deacon, but in case of necessity any person using true water and the Trinitarian form can validly baptize.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: Confirmation is the sacrament that strengthens and matures the spiritual life begun in Baptism, making the recipient a strong and perfect Christian and soldier of Jesus Christ.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Confirmation perfects baptismal grace, bringing spiritual maturity and strengthening the believer to act as a soldier of Jesus Christ.
passages.fullText: 1. Confirmation is the sacrament that strengthens and matures the spiritual life begun in Baptism, making the recipient a strong and perfect Christian and soldier of Jesus Christ.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: The matter of this sacrament is the anointing with holy chrism (consecrated olive oil and balsam) on the forehead accompanied by the imposition of hands by the Bishop (Acts 8:14-17).
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The sacramental matter of Confirmation comprises anointing with consecrated chrism on the forehead and the episcopal imposition of hands.
passages.fullText: 2. The matter of this sacrament is the anointing with holy chrism (consecrated olive oil and balsam) on the forehead accompanied by the imposition of hands by the Bishop (Acts 8:14-17).

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: The form consists of the words: "I sign thee with the sign of the Cross, and I confirm thee with the chrism of salvation, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The essential form of Confirmation invokes the Sign of the Cross, the chrism of salvation, and the Most Holy Trinity.
passages.fullText: 3. The form consists of the words: "I sign thee with the sign of the Cross, and I confirm thee with the chrism of salvation, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: It imprints an indelible character and imparts the sevenfold gifts of the Holy Ghost: Wisdom, Understanding, Counsel, Fortitude, Knowledge, Piety, and Fear of the Lord (Isaiah 11:2).
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Confirmation seals the recipient with an indelible spiritual character and bestows the sevenfold gifts of the Holy Ghost.
passages.fullText: 4. It imprints an indelible character and imparts the sevenfold gifts of the Holy Ghost: Wisdom, Understanding, Counsel, Fortitude, Knowledge, Piety, and Fear of the Lord (Isaiah 11:2).

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: The Holy Eucharist is the greatest of all sacraments, containing really, truly, and substantially the Body, Blood, Soul, and Divinity of our Lord Jesus Christ under the appearances of bread and wine.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Holy Eucharist is the preeminent sacrament because it contains the true, real, and substantial presence of Christ's Body, Blood, Soul, and Divinity under the species of bread and wine.
passages.fullText: 1. The Holy Eucharist is the greatest of all sacraments, containing really, truly, and substantially the Body, Blood, Soul, and Divinity of our Lord Jesus Christ under the appearances of bread and wine.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: At the Last Supper, Christ instituted this sublime sacrament and sacrifice when He took bread, blessed, broke, and gave it to His disciples, saying: "This is My Body,"
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christ instituted the Holy Eucharist at the Last Supper as both a sacrament and sacrifice of the New Covenant for the forgiveness of sins.
passages.fullText: 2. At the Last Supper, Christ instituted this sublime sacrament and sacrifice when He took bread, blessed, broke, and gave it to His disciples, saying: "This is My Body," and over the chalice: "This is My Blood of the new testament, which shall be shed for many unto remission of sins" (Matthew 26:26-28).

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: By the words of consecration spoken by the priest, the whole substance of the bread is converted into the Body of Christ, and the whole substance of the wine into His Blood, which marvelous change the Church terms Transubstantiation.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Transubstantiation is the complete conversion of the substance of bread and wine into the Body and Blood of Christ effected by the priest's words of consecration.
passages.fullText: 3. By the words of consecration spoken by the priest, the whole substance of the bread is converted into the Body of Christ, and the whole substance of the wine into His Blood, which marvelous change the Church terms Transubstantiation.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: The Eucharist is both a sacrament that nourishes the soul with divine life and the Holy Sacrifice of the Mass that perpetuates Calvary upon our altars (John 6:54).
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Eucharist simultaneously nourishes the soul with divine life as a sacrament and perpetuates the sacrifice of Calvary on the altar as the Mass.
passages.fullText: 4. The Eucharist is both a sacrament that nourishes the soul with divine life and the Holy Sacrifice of the Mass that perpetuates Calvary upon our altars (John 6:54).

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: Penance is the sacrament instituted by Christ for the forgiveness of sins committed after Baptism (John 20:23).
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Sacrament of Penance was instituted by Christ to provide spiritual healing and pardon for sins committed after Baptism.
passages.fullText: 1. Penance is the sacrament instituted by Christ for the forgiveness of sins committed after Baptism (John 20:23).

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: The essential acts of the penitent are three: Contrition (heartfelt sorrow for sin with purpose of amendment), Confession (sincere accusation of all mortal sins to an authorized priest), and Satisfaction (performance of the penance enjoined by the confessor).
passages.oneSentenceSummary: A valid reception of Penance requires three essential acts from the penitent: contrition, confession of mortal sins, and satisfaction.
passages.fullText: 2. The essential acts of the penitent are three: Contrition (heartfelt sorrow for sin with purpose of amendment), Confession (sincere accusation of all mortal sins to an authorized priest), and Satisfaction (performance of the penance enjoined by the confessor).

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: The form of the sacrament is the judicial absolution pronounced by the priest: "I absolve thee from thy sins in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The sacramental form of Penance is the judicial formula of absolution pronounced by the priest in the name of the Holy Trinity.
passages.fullText: 3. The form of the sacrament is the judicial absolution pronounced by the priest: "I absolve thee from thy sins in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: This sacrament restores sanctifying grace, reconciles the sinner with God and the Church, and revives merits lost through sin.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The effects of Penance include the restoration of sanctifying grace, ecclesial and divine reconciliation, and the revival of lost merits.
passages.fullText: 4. This sacrament restores sanctifying grace, reconciles the sinner with God and the Church, and revives merits lost through sin.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: Extreme Unction (the Anointing of the Sick) is the sacrament instituted by Christ to confer spiritual comfort, strength, and bodily relief to the faithful who are in danger of death through sickness or old age.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Extreme Unction provides spiritual comfort, fortitude, and physical relief for the faithful in proximate danger of death from sickness or aging.
passages.fullText: 1. Extreme Unction (the Anointing of the Sick) is the sacrament instituted by Christ to confer spiritual comfort, strength, and bodily relief to the faithful who are in danger of death through sickness or old age.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: "Is any man sick among you? Let him bring in the priests of the Church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord. And the prayer of faith shall save the sick man: and the Lord shall raise him up: and if he be in sins, they shall be forgiven him."
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Sacred Scripture through the Epistle of St. James explicitly attests to the apostolic practice of anointing the sick with oil by the priests for healing and forgiveness.
passages.fullText: 2. The Apostle James describes this sacrament in James 5:14-15: "Is any man sick among you? Let him bring in the priests of the Church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord. And the prayer of faith shall save the sick man: and the Lord shall raise him up: and if he be in sins, they shall be forgiven him."

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: It remits venial sins, cleanses remaining temporal punishment, strengthens the soul against final demonic assaults, and restores bodily health if expedient for the soul's salvation.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Extreme Unction cleanses venial sins and temporal punishment, fortifies against demonic temptation at the hour of death, and confers bodily healing when spiritually expedient.
passages.fullText: 3. It remits venial sins, cleanses remaining temporal punishment, strengthens the soul against final demonic assaults, and restores bodily health if expedient for the soul's salvation.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: Holy Orders is the sacrament by which spiritual power and grace are conferred upon bishops, priests, and deacons to exercise sacred liturgical ministries and shepherd the flock of Christ.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Holy Orders confers sacramental power and grace on the ordained hierarchy to conduct liturgical worship and pastor the Church.
passages.fullText: 1. Holy Orders is the sacrament by which spiritual power and grace are conferred upon bishops, priests, and deacons to exercise sacred liturgical ministries and shepherd the flock of Christ.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: The essential rite consists of the imposition of hands by the consecrating bishop and the solemn consecratory prayer (2 Timothy 1:6).
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The essential matter and form of Holy Orders consist in the bishop's laying on of hands and the solemn prayer of consecration.
passages.fullText: 2. The essential rite consists of the imposition of hands by the consecrating bishop and the solemn consecratory prayer (2 Timothy 1:6).

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: It imprints an indelible spiritual character upon the soul of the minister, configuring him to Christ the eternal High Priest and granting power to consecrate the Holy Eucharist and forgive sins.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Holy Orders imprints an indelible sacramental character configuring the ordained minister to Christ the High Priest and imparting sacred authority to consecrate the Eucharist and absolve sins.
passages.fullText: 3. It imprints an indelible spiritual character upon the soul of the minister, configuring him to Christ the eternal High Priest and granting power to consecrate the Holy Eucharist and forgive sins.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: Matrimony is the sacrament instituted by God in Paradise and elevated by Christ to sacramental dignity, uniting a Christian man and woman in an indissoluble bond of marital fidelity (Genesis 2:24; Matthew 19:6).
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Instituted in the state of innocence and elevated by Christ, Holy Matrimony establishes an indissoluble sacramental union of fidelity between husband and wife.
passages.fullText: 1. Matrimony is the sacrament instituted by God in Paradise and elevated by Christ to sacramental dignity, uniting a Christian man and woman in an indissoluble bond of marital fidelity (Genesis 2:24; Matthew 19:6).

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: It signifies the mystical union between Christ and His holy Church, as the Apostle Paul teaches in Ephesians 5:32: "This is a great sacrament; but I speak in Christ and in the Church."
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christian marriage serves as an efficacious sign and reflection of the mystical, unbreakable union between Christ and His Bride, the Church.
passages.fullText: 2. It signifies the mystical union between Christ and His holy Church, as the Apostle Paul teaches in Ephesians 5:32: "This is a great sacrament; but I speak in Christ and in the Church."

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: It confers special grace upon the spouses to live in mutual love, assist each other in holiness, and raise children in the fear and love of God.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Matrimony imparts actual and sanctifying grace enabling spouses to foster mutual charity, advance in Christian perfection, and faithfully educate their children in the love of God.
passages.fullText: 3. It confers special grace upon the spouses to live in mutual love, assist each other in holiness, and raise children in the fear and love of God.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: There are two ways, one of life and one of death, and there is a great difference between the two ways.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The fundamental moral and spiritual choice confronting humanity is between the Way of Life and the Way of Death.
passages.fullText: 1. There are two ways, one of life and one of death, and there is a great difference between the two ways.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: The way of life is this.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The teaching introduces the specific moral and spiritual precepts that constitute the Way of Life.
passages.fullText: 2. The way of life is this.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: First of all, thou shalt love the God that made thee;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The primary obligation and foundation of the Christian life is love of God, our Creator.
passages.fullText: 3. First of all, thou shalt love the God that made thee;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: secondly, thy neighbour as thyself.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The second great commandment of the Way of Life is to love one's neighbor as oneself.
passages.fullText: 4. secondly, thy neighbour as thyself.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And all things whatsoever thou wouldest not have befal thyself neither do thou unto another.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The negative formulation of the Golden Rule commands Christians to refrain from doing to others whatever they would not wish done to themselves.
passages.fullText: 5. And all things whatsoever thou wouldest not have befal thyself neither do thou unto another.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Now of these words the doctrine is this.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The text marks the transition to the specific apostolic doctrine and moral instructions expounding the Great Commandments.
passages.fullText: 6. Now of these words the doctrine is this.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Bless them that curse you, and pray for your enemies and fast for them that persecute you;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians are called to radical charity by blessing, praying for, and offering bodily penance on behalf of their persecutors and enemies.
passages.fullText: 7. Bless them that curse you, and pray for your enemies and fast for them that persecute you;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But do ye love them that hate you, and ye shall not have an enemy.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: True Christian charity exceeds pagan morality by actively loving those who hate us, thereby overcoming enmity through supernatural love.
passages.fullText: 8. for what thank is it, if ye love them that love you? Do not even the Gentiles the same? But do ye love them that hate you, and ye shall not have an enemy.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Abstain thou from fleshly and bodily lusts.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The disciple of Christ must maintain purity of heart and body by renouncing carnal desires and passions.
passages.fullText: 9. Abstain thou from fleshly and bodily lusts.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: If any man give thee a blow on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also, and thou shalt be perfect;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christian perfection entails heroic meekness and patient non-retaliation when enduring personal insults and injuries.
passages.fullText: 10. If any man give thee a blow on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also, and thou shalt be perfect;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: if a man impress thee to go with him, one mile, go with him twain;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The follower of Christ responds to unjust coercion and demands with generous humility and service beyond what is required.
passages.fullText: 11. if a man impress thee to go with him, one mile, go with him twain;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: if a man take away thy cloak, give him thy coat also;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Evangelical perfection requires complete detachment from material possessions and the peaceful surrender of earthly goods.
passages.fullText: 12. if a man take away thy cloak, give him thy coat also;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: if a man take away from thee that which is thine own, ask it not back, for neither art thou able.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians are called to radical detachment from earthly possessions and non-retaliation when deprived of their goods.
passages.fullText: 13. if a man take away from thee that which is thine own, ask it not back, for neither art thou able.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: To every man that asketh of thee give, and ask not back;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Way of Life requires universal generosity and open-handed charity without demanding repayment.
passages.fullText: 14. To every man that asketh of thee give, and ask not back;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for the Father desireth that gifts be given to all from His own bounties.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: God the Father wills that the bounties of His creation be freely shared among all people.
passages.fullText: 15. for the Father desireth that gifts be given to all from His own bounties.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Blessed is he that giveth according to the commandment;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Special beatitude and spiritual blessing belong to the believer who practices almsgiving in obedience to divine command.
passages.fullText: 16. Blessed is he that giveth according to the commandment;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for he is guiltless.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The faithful giver who shares according to God's commandment stands blameless before the Lord.
passages.fullText: 17. for he is guiltless.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Woe to him that receiveth;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: A severe spiritual warning is pronounced against those who receive charity deceitfully or covetously.
passages.fullText: 18. Woe to him that receiveth;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for, if a man receiveth having need, he is guiltless;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Those who receive alms out of genuine poverty incur no guilt or moral fault.
passages.fullText: 19. for, if a man receiveth having need, he is guiltless;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: but he that hath no need shall give satisfaction why and wherefore he received;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Anyone who takes charity without actual need will be held strictly accountable at judgment for their motives and actions.
passages.fullText: 20. but he that hath no need shall give satisfaction why and wherefore he received;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: and being put in confinement he shall be examined concerning the deeds that he hath done, and he shall not come out thence until he hath given back the last farthing.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Those who exploit charity will undergo rigorous examination and detention until full satisfaction and restitution are rendered.
passages.fullText: 21. and being put in confinement he shall be examined concerning the deeds that he hath done, and he shall not come out thence until he hath given back the last farthing.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Yea, as touching this also it is said;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The text appeals to authoritative traditional wisdom concerning the practice of almsgiving.
passages.fullText: 22. Yea, as touching this also it is said;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Let thine alms sweat into thine hands, until thou shalt have learnt to whom to give.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians are instructed to exercise prudence, sweat, and careful discernment before dispensing their alms.
passages.fullText: 23. Let thine alms sweat into thine hands, until thou shalt have learnt to whom to give.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And after ye are satisfied thus give ye thanks:
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache instructs the faithful on the proper liturgical thanksgiving to offer immediately following the reception of Holy Communion.
passages.fullText: 1. And after ye are satisfied thus give ye thanks:

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: We give Thee thanks, Holy Father, for Thy holy name, which Thou hast made to tabernacle in our hearts, and for the knowledge and faith and immortality, which Thou hast made known unto us through Thy Son Jesus;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The post-Communion thanksgiving praises the Father for the indwelling of His Holy Name in believers' hearts and for the gifts of faith, divine knowledge, and immortality revealed in Christ.
passages.fullText: 2. We give Thee thanks, Holy Father, for Thy holy name, which Thou hast made to tabernacle in our hearts, and for the knowledge and faith and immortality, which Thou hast made known unto us through Thy Son Jesus;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thine is the glory for ever and ever.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: A solemn liturgical doxology rendering perpetual glory and worship to God.
passages.fullText: 3. Thine is the glory for ever and ever.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou, Almighty Master, didst create all things for Thy name's sake, and didst give food and drink unto men for enjoyment, that they might render thanks to Thee;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: God the Almighty Creator made the universe for His glory and graciously provided material food and drink to sustain mankind and elicit grateful praise.
passages.fullText: 4. Thou, Almighty Master, didst create all things for Thy name's sake, and didst give food and drink unto men for enjoyment, that they might render thanks to Thee;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: but didst bestow upon us spiritual food and drink and eternal life through Thy Son.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Beyond natural sustenance, God bestows the supernatural grace of spiritual food, drink, and eternal life upon believers through His Son in the Eucharist.
passages.fullText: 5. but didst bestow upon us spiritual food and drink and eternal life through Thy Son.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Before all things we give Thee thanks that Thou art powerful;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Eucharistic prayer renders primary thanksgiving to God for His transcendent, sovereign omnipotence.
passages.fullText: 6. Before all things we give Thee thanks that Thou art powerful;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thine is the glory for ever and ever.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: A recurring liturgical acclamation acknowledging the eternal majesty and glory belonging to God alone.
passages.fullText: 7. Thine is the glory for ever and ever.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Remember, Lord, Thy Church to deliver it from all evil and to perfect it in Thy love;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Church petitions the Lord for divine preservation against all evil and for her sanctification and perfection in charity.
passages.fullText: 8. Remember, Lord, Thy Church to deliver it from all evil and to perfect it in Thy love;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: and gather it together from the four winds—even the Church which has been sanctified—into Thy kingdom which Thou hast prepared for it;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The liturgy asks God to gather His holy and unified Church from every corner of the earth into the eternal Kingdom prepared for her.
passages.fullText: 9. and gather it together from the four winds—even the Church which has been sanctified—into Thy kingdom which Thou hast prepared for it;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for Thine is the power and the glory for ever and ever.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: A concluding Eucharistic doxology affirming that everlasting power and glory belong to God.
passages.fullText: 10. for Thine is the power and the glory for ever and ever.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: May grace come and may this world pass away.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: An eschatological longing and prayer for the coming of divine grace and the passing away of the temporal world in anticipation of the eternal Kingdom.
passages.fullText: 11. May grace come and may this world pass away.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Hosanna to the God of David.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: A liturgical Eucharistic acclamation hailing Christ as the divine fulfillment of the Davidic promises.
passages.fullText: 12. Hosanna to the God of David.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: If any man is holy, let him come;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Only those who are sanctified and in a state of grace are invited to approach and receive the Most Holy Eucharist.
passages.fullText: 13. If any man is holy, let him come;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: if any man is not, let him repent. Maran Atha. Amen.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Those conscious of sin must repent before approaching the Eucharistic mystery in anticipation of the Lord's coming.
passages.fullText: 14. if any man is not, let him repent. Maran Atha. Amen.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But permit the prophets to offer thanksgiving as much as they desire.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Prophets in the early Christian assembly are permitted freedom to offer extensive Eucharistic prayers of thanksgiving as the Spirit moves them.
passages.fullText: 15. But permit the prophets to offer thanksgiving as much as they desire.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Whosoever therefore shall come and teach you all these things that have been said before, receive him;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The faithful must welcome and receive any minister who faithfully hands on the authentic doctrine of the Apostolic Tradition.
passages.fullText: 1. Whosoever therefore shall come and teach you all these things that have been said before, receive him;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: but if the teacher himself be perverted and teach a different doctrine to the destruction thereof, hear him not;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians are bound to reject any teacher who perverts sound doctrine and spreads destructive errors contrary to apostolic faith.
passages.fullText: 2. but if the teacher himself be perverted and teach a different doctrine to the destruction thereof, hear him not;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: but if to the increase of righteousness and the knowledge of the Lord, receive him as the Lord.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Teachers whose instruction fosters righteousness and the knowledge of God are to be reverenced as the Lord Himself.
passages.fullText: 3. but if to the increase of righteousness and the knowledge of the Lord, receive him as the Lord.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But concerning the apostles and prophets, so do ye according to the ordinance of the Gospel.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Church's discernment and reception of traveling apostles and prophets must conform strictly to the standard of the Gospel.
passages.fullText: 4. But concerning the apostles and prophets, so do ye according to the ordinance of the Gospel.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Let every apostle, when he cometh to you, be received as the Lord;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Authentic apostolic emissaries are to be received with the honor and hospitality due to Christ Himself.
passages.fullText: 5. Let every apostle, when he cometh to you, be received as the Lord;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: but he shall not abide more than a single day, or if there be need, a second likewise;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Itinerant ministers are to maintain their missionary momentum and not linger beyond one or two days in any single community.
passages.fullText: 6. but he shall not abide more than a single day, or if there be need, a second likewise;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: but if he abide three days, he is a false prophet.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Lingering to exploit a local congregation's hospitality exposes an itinerant traveler as a false prophet.
passages.fullText: 7. but if he abide three days, he is a false prophet.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And when he departeth let the apostle receive nothing save bread, until he findeth shelter;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: True apostolic laborers practice evangelical poverty, accepting only necessary daily food for their continuing mission.
passages.fullText: 8. And when he departeth let the apostle receive nothing save bread, until he findeth shelter;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: but if he ask money, he is a false prophet.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Demanding monetary payment for spiritual ministry unmasks a preacher as a counterfeit prophet motivated by worldly greed.
passages.fullText: 9. but if he ask money, he is a false prophet.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And any prophet speaking in the Spirit ye shall not try neither discern;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache commands reverence toward genuine utterances of the Holy Spirit, warning against rashly testing authentic prophetic charisms.
passages.fullText: 10. And any prophet speaking in the Spirit ye shall not try neither discern;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for every sin shall be forgiven, but this sin shall not be forgiven.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Reflecting the Gospel teaching on blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, the Didache warns of the uniquely severe gravity of resisting the Spirit.
passages.fullText: 11. for every sin shall be forgiven, but this sin shall not be forgiven.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Yet not every one that speaketh in the Spirit is a prophet, but only if he have the ways of the Lord.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: True prophetic authenticity requires not merely ecstatic speech, but a life fully conforming to the character and commandments of Christ.
passages.fullText: 12. Yet not every one that speaketh in the Spirit is a prophet, but only if he have the ways of the Lord.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: From his ways therefore the false prophet and the prophet shall be recognized.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: A person's moral conduct and daily way of life serve as the indispensable criteria for discerning true prophets from deceivers.
passages.fullText: 13. From his ways therefore the false prophet and the prophet shall be recognized.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And no prophet when he ordereth a table in the Spirit shall eat of it;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: A prophet who orders a meal for the poor under inspiration must not partake of it himself, guarding against self-serving spiritual abuse.
passages.fullText: 14. And no prophet when he ordereth a table in the Spirit shall eat of it;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: otherwise he is a false prophet.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Any minister who exploits spiritual authority for personal physical gratification reveals himself to be a false prophet.
passages.fullText: 15. otherwise he is a false prophet.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And every prophet teaching the truth, if he doeth not what he teacheth, is a false prophet.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Authentic Christian ministry demands moral integrity, as teaching correct doctrine while failing to practice it unmasks a false prophet.
passages.fullText: 16. And every prophet teaching the truth, if he doeth not what he teacheth, is a false prophet.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And every prophet approved and found true, if he doeth ought as an outward mystery typical of the Church, and yet teacheth you not to do all that he himself doeth, shall not be judged before you;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The faithful are instructed not to judge true prophets who enact symbolic actions representative of the Church's mystery without imposing those unique actions on the congregation.
passages.fullText: 17. And every prophet approved and found true, if he doeth ought as an outward mystery typical of the Church, and yet teacheth you not to do all that he himself doeth, shall not be judged before you;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: he hath his judgment in the presence of God;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The ultimate evaluation and accountability of an approved minister of the Church rests directly in the judgment of God.
passages.fullText: 18. he hath his judgment in the presence of God;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for in like manner also did the prophets of old time.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The symbolic and mysterious actions of Christian prophets stand in direct continuity with the prophetic traditions of the Old Testament.
passages.fullText: 19. for in like manner also did the prophets of old time.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And whosoever shall say in the Spirit, Give me silver or anything else, ye shall not listen to him;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache warns believers to reject any supposed prophet who demands money or material possessions for personal benefit under the guise of spiritual inspiration.
passages.fullText: 20. And whosoever shall say in the Spirit, Give me silver or anything else, ye shall not listen to him;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: but if he tell you to give on behalf of others that are in want, let no man judge him.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: A minister who solicits charity and alms purely on behalf of the destitute is commendable and above suspicion.
passages.fullText: 21. but if he tell you to give on behalf of others that are in want, let no man judge him.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But let every one that cometh in the name of the Lord be received;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache instructs the Christian community to extend open hospitality and welcome to anyone who comes in the name of the Lord.
passages.fullText: 1. But let every one that cometh in the name of the Lord be received;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: and then when ye have tested him ye shall know him, for ye shall have understanding on the right hand and on the left.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Believers are urged to exercise spiritual discernment and prudent testing to evaluate the authenticity and motives of visiting travelers.
passages.fullText: 2. and then when ye have tested him ye shall know him, for ye shall have understanding on the right hand and on the left.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: If the comer is a traveller, assist him, so far as ye are able;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians are called to perform corporal works of mercy by aiding traveling brethren according to their means.
passages.fullText: 3. If the comer is a traveller, assist him, so far as ye are able;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: but he shall not stay with you more than two or three days, if it be necessary.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The early Church placed prudent time limits on hospitality to prevent itinerant guests from taking unfair advantage of Christian charity.
passages.fullText: 4. but he shall not stay with you more than two or three days, if it be necessary.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But if he wishes to settle with you, being a craftsman, let him work for and eat his bread.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache affirms the dignity of manual labor, requiring any visiting craftsman seeking to settle in the community to earn his own sustenance.
passages.fullText: 5. But if he wishes to settle with you, being a craftsman, let him work for and eat his bread.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But if he has no craft, according to your wisdom provide how he shall live as a Christian among you, but not in idleness.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The community is tasked with finding honest occupation for unskilled newcomers so that no Christian lives in spiritual or social idleness.
passages.fullText: 6. But if he has no craft, according to your wisdom provide how he shall live as a Christian among you, but not in idleness.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: If he will not do this, he is trafficking upon Christ.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Refusing to work and instead exploiting the charity of the Church is condemned as a grave sin of trafficking upon the name of Christ.
passages.fullText: 7. If he will not do this, he is trafficking upon Christ.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Beware of such men.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The faithful are explicitly warned to remain vigilant against dishonest opportunists who abuse the faith for material gain.
passages.fullText: 8. Beware of such men.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But every true prophet desiring to settle among you is worthy of his food.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Genuine prophets and ministers dedicated to building up the local Church are worthy of material support and sustenance from the faithful.
passages.fullText: 1. But every true prophet desiring to settle among you is worthy of his food.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: In like manner a true teacher is also worthy, like the workman, of his food.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Authentic teachers of Catholic doctrine are entitled to sustenance, affirming the principle that those who minister the Gospel are worthy of their livelihood.
passages.fullText: 2. In like manner a true teacher is also worthy, like the workman, of his food.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Every firstfruit then of the produce of the wine-vat and of the threshing-floor, of thy oxen and of thy sheep, thou shalt take and give as the firstfruit to the prophets;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The faithful are commanded to tithe the firstfruits of their agricultural labor and flocks to support the Church's prophets and ministers.
passages.fullText: 3. Every firstfruit then of the produce of the wine-vat and of the threshing-floor, of thy oxen and of thy sheep, thou shalt take and give as the firstfruit to the prophets;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for they are your chief-priests.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache identifies the authentic ministers and prophets as chief priests within the Christian community, justifying their reception of the firstfruits.
passages.fullText: 4. for they are your chief-priests.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But if ye have not a prophet, give them to the poor.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: When no resident prophet or teacher is present to receive the firstfruits, they must be given as alms to the poor.
passages.fullText: 5. But if ye have not a prophet, give them to the poor.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: If thou makest bread, take the firstfruit and give according to the commandment.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Believers are instructed to set aside the first portion of their daily bread as an offering in obedience to God's law.
passages.fullText: 6. If thou makest bread, take the firstfruit and give according to the commandment.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: In like manner, when thou openest a jar of wine or of oil, take the firstfruit and give to the prophets;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The firstfruits of provisions such as wine and oil are to be given dutifully for the material support of the prophets.
passages.fullText: 7. In like manner, when thou openest a jar of wine or of oil, take the firstfruit and give to the prophets;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: yea and of money and raiment and every possession take the firstfruit, as shall seem good to thee, and give according to the commandment.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians are called to exercise detachment and generosity by offering the first portion of all their money, clothing, and possessions.
passages.fullText: 8. yea and of money and raiment and every possession take the firstfruit, as shall seem good to thee, and give according to the commandment.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And on the Lord's own day gather yourselves together and break bread and give thanks, first confessing your transgressions, that your sacrifice may be pure.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The faithful must gather on Sunday to offer the Eucharistic sacrifice of thanksgiving, confessing their sins beforehand so that their offering is pure.
passages.fullText: 1. And on the Lord's own day gather yourselves together and break bread and give thanks, first confessing your transgressions, that your sacrifice may be pure.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And let no man, having his dispute with his fellow, join your assembly until they have been reconciled, that your sacrifice may not be defiled;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Fraternal reconciliation is an essential prerequisite for participating in the Eucharistic assembly so that the sacrifice remains undefiled.
passages.fullText: 2. And let no man, having his dispute with his fellow, join your assembly until they have been reconciled, that your sacrifice may not be defiled;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for this sacrifice it is that was spoken of by the Lord:
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Sunday Eucharistic assembly is identified as the very sacrifice foretold in Sacred Scripture by the Lord.
passages.fullText: 3. for this sacrifice it is that was spoken of by the Lord:

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: In every place and at every time offer Me a pure sacrifice;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The prophetic command demands a pure Eucharistic sacrifice offered perpetually across all times and places.
passages.fullText: 4. In every place and at every time offer Me a pure sacrifice;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for I am a great king, saith the Lord and My name is wonderful among the nations.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: God reveals His sovereign divine majesty and universal kingship, declaring His name to be exalted among all peoples.
passages.fullText: 5. for I am a great king, saith the Lord and My name is wonderful among the nations.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Appoint for yourselves therefore bishops and deacons worthy of the Lord, men who are meek and not lovers of money, and true and approved;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Church must appoint bishops and deacons of proven virtue, meekness, honesty, and financial detachment to shepherd the faithful.
passages.fullText: 1. Appoint for yourselves therefore bishops and deacons worthy of the Lord, men who are meek and not lovers of money, and true and approved;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for unto you they also perform the service of the prophets and teachers.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Bishops and deacons are to be honored because they carry out the liturgical and pedagogical ministry of prophets and teachers in the community.
passages.fullText: 2. for unto you they also perform the service of the prophets and teachers.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Therefore despise them not;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The faithful are strictly enjoined not to despise their ordained local ministers but to give them proper honor.
passages.fullText: 3. Therefore despise them not;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for they are your honourable men along with the prophets and teachers.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Bishops and deacons are to be held in equal honor alongside prophets and teachers as legitimate ministers of the Church.
passages.fullText: 4. for they are your honourable men along with the prophets and teachers.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And reprove one another, not in anger but in peace, as ye find in the Gospel;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Fraternal correction must always be administered in peaceful charity rather than wrath, in accordance with the Gospel.
passages.fullText: 5. And reprove one another, not in anger but in peace, as ye find in the Gospel;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: and let no one speak to any that has gone wrong towards his neighbour, neither let him hear a word from you, until he repent.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Ecclesial discipline requires withholding fellowship from an unrepentant offender until true contrition and reconciliation are achieved.
passages.fullText: 6. and let no one speak to any that has gone wrong towards his neighbour, neither let him hear a word from you, until he repent.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But your prayers and your almsgivings and all your deeds so do ye as ye find it in the Gospel of our Lord.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: All prayers, charitable giving, and Christian actions must be patterned faithfully upon the teaching of the Gospel.
passages.fullText: 7. But your prayers and your almsgivings and all your deeds so do ye as ye find it in the Gospel of our Lord.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Be watchful for your life;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians are exhorted to maintain constant spiritual vigilance over their souls in anticipation of the Lord's return.
passages.fullText: 1. Be watchful for your life;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: let your lamps not be quenched and your loins not ungirded, but be ye ready;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Believers must keep their spiritual lamps burning and remain actively prepared for the Parousia.
passages.fullText: 2. let your lamps not be quenched and your loins not ungirded, but be ye ready;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for ye know not the hour in which our Lord cometh.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The uncertainty of the exact hour of Christ's return demands continual readiness and holy living.
passages.fullText: 3. for ye know not the hour in which our Lord cometh.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And ye shall gather yourselves together frequently, seeking what is fitting for your souls;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Frequent communal assembly is essential for edifying the faithful and securing the salvation of their souls.
passages.fullText: 4. And ye shall gather yourselves together frequently, seeking what is fitting for your souls;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for the whole time of your faith shall not profit you, if ye be not perfected at the last season.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Lifelong faith is of no eternal benefit without final perseverance and perfection in grace at the end.
passages.fullText: 5. for the whole time of your faith shall not profit you, if ye be not perfected at the last season.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: For in the last days the false prophets and corrupters shall be multiplied, and the sheep shall be turned into wolves, and love shall be turned into hate.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The end times will be characterized by the multiplication of deceivers, the apostasy of believers, and the perversion of charity into malice.
passages.fullText: 6. For in the last days the false prophets and corrupters shall be multiplied, and the sheep shall be turned into wolves, and love shall be turned into hate.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: For as lawlessness increaseth, they shall hate one another and shall persecute and betray.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The escalation of iniquity in the final days will lead to widespread hatred, mutual betrayal, and severe persecution.
passages.fullText: 7. For as lawlessness increaseth, they shall hate one another and shall persecute and betray.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And then the world-deceiver shall appear as a son of God;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The ultimate eschatological tribulation includes the appearance of the Antichrist, who blasphemously masquerades as the Son of God.
passages.fullText: 8. And then the world-deceiver shall appear as a son of God;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: and shall work signs and wonders, and the earth shall be delivered into his hands;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: In the end times, the deceiver of the world will perform false signs and wonders to lead humanity astray.
passages.fullText: 9. and shall work signs and wonders, and the earth shall be delivered into his hands;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: and he shall do unholy things, which have never been since the world began.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The eschatological deceiver will commit unprecedented acts of lawlessness and iniquity against God and His creation.
passages.fullText: 10. and he shall do unholy things, which have never been since the world began.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Then all created mankind shall come to the fire of testing, and many shall be offended and perish;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Humanity will undergo a severe furnace of trial in the final days, causing many to stumble and fall away.
passages.fullText: 11. Then all created mankind shall come to the fire of testing, and many shall be offended and perish;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: but they that endure in their faith shall be saved by the Curse Himself.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Those who persevere in theological faith through trials will attain salvation through Christ, who became a curse for our redemption.
passages.fullText: 12. but they that endure in their faith shall be saved by the Curse Himself.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And then shall the signs of the truth appear;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Following the great tribulation, the authentic signs of divine truth will appear to inaugurate the Parousia.
passages.fullText: 13. And then shall the signs of the truth appear;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: first a sign of a rift in the heaven, then a sign of a voice of a trumpet, and thirdly a resurrection of the dead;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The final arrival of the Kingdom will be heralded by the opening of the heavens, the angelic trumpet, and the bodily resurrection of the dead.
passages.fullText: 14. first a sign of a rift in the heaven, then a sign of a voice of a trumpet, and thirdly a resurrection of the dead;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: yet not of all, but as it was said:
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The author appeals to prophetic Sacred Scripture to explain the nature of the first resurrection of the righteous at the Parousia.
passages.fullText: 15. yet not of all, but as it was said:

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: The Lord shall come and all His saints with Him.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Lord Jesus Christ will return in glory accompanied by the communion of all His holy angels and saints.
passages.fullText: 16. The Lord shall come and all His saints with Him.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Then shall the world see the Lord coming upon the clouds of heaven.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Human history will culminate in the visible, glorious return of the Lord on the clouds of heaven to judge the living and the dead.
passages.fullText: 17. Then shall the world see the Lord coming upon the clouds of heaven.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And this is the second commandment of the teaching.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache introduces the second section of apostolic moral catechesis containing specific prohibitions and duties.
passages.fullText: 1. And this is the second commandment of the teaching.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: thou shalt not murder a child by abortion nor kill them when born, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's goods,
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache outlines essential moral prohibitions for Christians, forbidding murder, abortion, infanticide, sexual immorality, theft, sorcery, perjury, and malice.
passages.fullText: 2. Thou shalt do no murder, thou shalt not commit adultery, thou shalt not corrupt boys, thou shalt not commit fornication, thou shalt not steal, thou shalt not deal in magic, thou shalt do no sorcery, thou shalt not murder a child by abortion nor kill them when born, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's goods, thou shalt not perjure thyself, thou shalt not bear false witness, thou shalt not speak evil, thou shalt not cherish a grudge, thou shalt not be double-minded nor double-tongued;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for the double tongue is a snare of death.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Duplicity and deceitful speech are warned against as deadly traps leading to spiritual ruin.
passages.fullText: 3. for the double tongue is a snare of death.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thy word shall not be false or empty, but fulfilled by action.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christian speech must be characterized by truthfulness and matched by righteous deeds.
passages.fullText: 4. Thy word shall not be false or empty, but fulfilled by action.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou shalt not be avaricious nor a plunderer nor a hypocrite nor ill-tempered nor proud.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Believers are commanded to reject the capital vices of greed, hypocrisy, anger, and pride.
passages.fullText: 5. Thou shalt not be avaricious nor a plunderer nor a hypocrite nor ill-tempered nor proud.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou shalt not entertain an evil design against thy neighbour.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Charity requires rooting out all internal malice and premeditated harm directed toward one's neighbor.
passages.fullText: 6. Thou shalt not entertain an evil design against thy neighbour.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou shalt not hate any man, but some thou shalt reprove, and for others thou shalt pray, and others thou shalt love more than thy life.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians must reject all hatred, practicing fraternal correction, intercessory prayer, and sacrificial love for others.
passages.fullText: 7. Thou shalt not hate any man, but some thou shalt reprove, and for others thou shalt pray, and others thou shalt love more than thy life.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: My child, flee from every evil and everything that resembleth it.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The spiritual disciple must strictly avoid not only blatant sin, but also all near occasions and appearances of evil.
passages.fullText: 1. My child, flee from every evil and everything that resembleth it.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Be not angry, for anger leadeth to murder, nor jealous nor contentious nor wrathful;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Passions of anger, jealousy, and contention must be checked at their inception because they logically culminate in murder.
passages.fullText: 2. Be not angry, for anger leadeth to murder, nor jealous nor contentious nor wrathful;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for of all these things murders are engendered.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Unchecked internal wrath and strife are the spiritual seeds from which violent external crimes arise.
passages.fullText: 3. for of all these things murders are engendered.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: My child, be not lustful, for lust leadeth to fornication, neither foul-speaking neither with uplifted eyes;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Preserving chastity requires custody of the eyes, clean speech, and guarding against the initial movements of lust.
passages.fullText: 4. My child, be not lustful, for lust leadeth to fornication, neither foul-speaking neither with uplifted eyes;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for of all these things adulteries are engendered.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Immodest glances, impure speech, and harbored lusts inevitably breed the grave sin of adultery.
passages.fullText: 5. for of all these things adulteries are engendered.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: My child, be no dealer in omens, since it leads to idolatry, nor an enchanter nor an astrologer nor a magician,
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache strictly forbids divination, astrology, and magic because occult practices seduce the soul into idolatry.
passages.fullText: 6. My child, be no dealer in omens, since it leads to idolatry, nor an enchanter nor an astrologer nor a magician, neither be willing to look at them;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for from all these things idolatry is engendered.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The text warns that superstitious and occult practices serve as spiritual gateways from which full idolatry is engendered.
passages.fullText: 7. for from all these things idolatry is engendered.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: My child, be not a liar, since lying leads to theft, neither avaricious neither vainglorious;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Counsel is given against falsehood, greed, and vanity, identifying them as dangerous precursors to the sin of theft.
passages.fullText: 8. My child, be not a liar, since lying leads to theft, neither avaricious neither vainglorious;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for from all these things thefts are engendered.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The passage warns that lying, avarice, and vainglory inevitably give birth to theft.
passages.fullText: 9. for from all these things thefts are engendered.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: My child, be not a murmurer, since it leadeth to blasphemy, neither self-willed neither a thinker of evil thoughts;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The believer is exhorted to shun grumbling, obstinacy, and malicious thoughts because they lead directly to blasphemy.
passages.fullText: 10. My child, be not a murmurer, since it leadeth to blasphemy, neither self-willed neither a thinker of evil thoughts;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for from all these things blasphemies are engendered.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The text cautions that inner discontent, self-will, and malicious thoughts are the fertile ground from which blasphemies arise.
passages.fullText: 11. for from all these things blasphemies are engendered.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But be meek, since the meek shall inherit the earth.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Echoing Christ's Beatitudes, the text commands the practice of meekness and promises the inheritance of the earth.
passages.fullText: 12. But be meek, since the meek shall inherit the earth.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Be long-suffering and pitiful and guileless and quiet and kindly and always fearing the words which thou hast heard.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians are instructed to cultivate patience, compassion, simplicity, peaceableness, and a reverent awe before the word of God.
passages.fullText: 13. Be long-suffering and pitiful and guileless and quiet and kindly and always fearing the words which thou hast heard.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou shalt not exalt thyself, neither shalt thou admit boldness into thy soul.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The passage forbids pride and presumption, commanding the soul to avoid self-exaltation and arrogant boldness.
passages.fullText: 14. Thou shalt not exalt thyself, neither shalt thou admit boldness into thy soul.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thy soul shall not cleave together with the lofty, but with the righteous and humble shalt thou walk.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Christian is called to reject companionship with the proud and walk in fellowship with the righteous and humble.
passages.fullText: 15. Thy soul shall not cleave together with the lofty, but with the righteous and humble shalt thou walk.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: The accidents that befal thee thou shalt receive as good, knowing that nothing is done without God.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The faithful are taught to accept all circumstances and trials as good, recognizing the sovereign, all-embracing providence of God.
passages.fullText: 16. The accidents that befal thee thou shalt receive as good, knowing that nothing is done without God.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: My child, thou shalt remember him that speaketh unto thee the word of God night and day, and shalt honour him as the Lord;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The faithful are commanded to remember and revere their spiritual pastors and teachers who preach God's word as representatives of the Lord.
passages.fullText: 1. My child, thou shalt remember him that speaketh unto thee the word of God night and day, and shalt honour him as the Lord;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for whencesoever the Lordship speaketh, there is the Lord.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christ the Lord is truly present wherever His divine authority and saving teaching are proclaimed.
passages.fullText: 2. for whencesoever the Lordship speaketh, there is the Lord.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Moreover thou shalt seek out day by day the persons of the saints, that thou mayest find rest in their words.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Believers are exhorted to daily seek the fellowship and counsel of holy Christians to find spiritual consolation and edification in their words.
passages.fullText: 3. Moreover thou shalt seek out day by day the persons of the saints, that thou mayest find rest in their words.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou shalt not make a schism, but thou shalt pacify them that contend;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache forbids schism and commands Christians to be active peacemakers among those in dispute to preserve ecclesial unity.
passages.fullText: 4. Thou shalt not make a schism, but thou shalt pacify them that contend;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: thou shalt judge righteously, thou shalt not make a difference in a person to reprove him for transgressions.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Fraternal correction and moral judgments must be carried out righteously and impartially, without showing favoritism or respect of persons.
passages.fullText: 5. thou shalt judge righteously, thou shalt not make a difference in a person to reprove him for transgressions.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou shalt not doubt whether a thing shall be or not be.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians are called to steadfast faith and unhesitating trust in God's providence, avoiding spiritual wavering and double-minded doubt.
passages.fullText: 6. Thou shalt not doubt whether a thing shall be or not be.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Be not thou found holding out thy hands to receive, but drawing them in as to giving.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The disciple of Christ must cultivate an openhanded spirit of generosity rather than a selfish posture of eager receiving and grudging giving.
passages.fullText: 7. Be not thou found holding out thy hands to receive, but drawing them in as to giving.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: If thou hast ought passing through thy hands, thou shalt give a ransom for thy sins.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: In accordance with patristic theology, almsgiving from one's possessions serves as an expiatory work and spiritual remedy for sin.
passages.fullText: 8. If thou hast ought passing through thy hands, thou shalt give a ransom for thy sins.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou shalt not hesitate to give, neither shalt thou murmur when giving;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Almsgiving must be offered promptly and with a cheerful heart, free from hesitation, reluctance, or complaining.
passages.fullText: 9. Thou shalt not hesitate to give, neither shalt thou murmur when giving;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for thou shalt know who is the good paymaster of thy reward.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Generosity is grounded in the assurance that God is the just and bountiful recompenser of every good work done for His sake.
passages.fullText: 10. for thou shalt know who is the good paymaster of thy reward.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou shalt not turn away from him that is in want, but shalt make thy brother partaker in all things, and shalt not say that anything is thine own.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Early Christian charity demands radical solidarity with the poor and the sharing of material goods without claiming exclusive ownership.
passages.fullText: 11. Thou shalt not turn away from him that is in want, but shalt make thy brother partaker in all things, and shalt not say that anything is thine own.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou shalt not withhold thy hand from thy son or from thy daughter, but from their youth thou shalt teach them the fear of God.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Sharing spiritual and earthly goods extends to the domestic church, where parents are commanded to raise and discipline their children in the fear of God.
passages.fullText: 12. For if ye are fellow-partakers in that which is imperishable, how much rather in the things which are perishable? Thou shalt not withhold thy hand from thy son or from thy daughter, but from their youth thou shalt teach them the fear of God.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou shalt not command thy bondservant or thine handmaid in thy bitterness, who trust in the same God as thyself, lest haply they should cease to fear the God who is over both of you;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christian masters are forbidden from treating servants harshly, recognizing their shared spiritual equality under the one God and Master of all.
passages.fullText: 13. Thou shalt not command thy bondservant or thine handmaid in thy bitterness, who trust in the same God as thyself, lest haply they should cease to fear the God who is over both of you;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for He cometh, not to call men with respect of persons, but He cometh to those whom the Spirit hath prepared.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: God’s sovereign call is impartial toward earthly status, calling all those whom the Holy Spirit has interiorly disposed and prepared by grace.
passages.fullText: 14. for He cometh, not to call men with respect of persons, but He cometh to those whom the Spirit hath prepared.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But ye, servants, shall be subject unto your masters, as to a type of God, in shame and fear.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christian servants are called to fulfill their daily duties by submitting to their masters with reverence and humility as an earthly reflection of divine authority.
passages.fullText: 15. But ye, servants, shall be subject unto your masters, as to a type of God, in shame and fear.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou shalt hate all hypocrisy, and everything that is not pleasing to the Lord.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Christian must utterly renounce hypocrisy and avoid anything contrary to the will and pleasure of God.
passages.fullText: 16. Thou shalt hate all hypocrisy, and everything that is not pleasing to the Lord.
