passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou shalt never forsake the commandments of the Lord;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Believers are commanded to maintain unwavering fidelity and obedience to the Lord's moral commandments.
passages.fullText: 17. Thou shalt never forsake the commandments of the Lord;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: but shalt keep those things which thou hast received, neither adding to them nor taking away from them.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Apostolic Tradition must be guarded intact, preserved faithfully without addition or subtraction.
passages.fullText: 18. but shalt keep those things which thou hast received, neither adding to them nor taking away from them.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: In church thou shalt confess thy transgressions, and shalt not betake thyself to prayer with an evil conscience.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The faithful are instructed to confess their sins within the ecclesial assembly so as not to approach prayer with a defiled conscience.
passages.fullText: 19. In church thou shalt confess thy transgressions, and shalt not betake thyself to prayer with an evil conscience.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: This is the way of life.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Living according to these divine precepts constitutes the true path of supernatural life and salvation.
passages.fullText: 20. This is the way of life.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But the way of death is this.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The text introduces the 'Way of Death', summarizing the path of sin that leads to spiritual ruin and eternal damnation.
passages.fullText: 1. But the way of death is this.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: First of all, it is evil and full of a curse: murders, adulteries, lusts, fornications, thefts, idolatries, magical arts, witchcrafts, plunderings, false witnessings, hypocrisies...
passages.oneSentenceSummary: A comprehensive catalogue of vices—including idolatry, murder, impurity, occultism, and pride—illustrates the cursed nature of mortal sin.
passages.fullText: 2. First of all, it is evil and full of a curse: murders, adulteries, lusts, fornications, thefts, idolatries, magical arts, witchcrafts, plunderings, false witnessings, hypocrisies, doubleness of heart, treachery, pride, malice, stubbornness, covetousness, foul-speaking, jealousy, boldness, exaltation, boastfulness;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: persecutors of good men, hating truth, loving a lie, not perceiving the reward of righteousness, not cleaving to the good nor to righteous judgment...
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Those walking the way of death oppose truth, persecute the righteous, and remain blind to God's eternal rewards.
passages.fullText: 3. persecutors of good men, hating truth, loving a lie, not perceiving the reward of righteousness, not cleaving to the good nor to righteous judgment, wakeful not for that which is good but for that which is evil;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: from whom gentleness and forbearance stand aloof;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Those ensnared in evil are utterly devoid of the Christian virtues of meekness, gentleness, and patient forbearance.
passages.fullText: 4. from whom gentleness and forbearance stand aloof;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: not pitying the poor man, not toiling for him that is oppressed with toil, not recognizing Him that made them, murderers of children, corrupters of the creatures of God...
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The way of death is characterized by cold indifference to the poor, violent disregard for unborn human life, and willful rebellion against the Creator.
passages.fullText: 5. loving vain things, pursuing a recompense, not pitying the poor man, not toiling for him that is oppressed with toil, not recognizing Him that made them, murderers of children, corrupters of the creatures of God, turning away from him that is in want, oppressing him that is afflicted, advocates of the wealthy, unjust judges of the poor, altogether sinful.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: May ye be delivered, my children, from all these things.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The author concludes the warning against the way of death with a pastoral blessing praying for the spiritual deliverance and protection of the faithful.
passages.fullText: 6. May ye be delivered, my children, from all these things.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: See lest any man lead you astray from this way of righteousness, for he teacheth thee apart from God.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Believers are warned against false teachers who deviate from the apostolic way of righteousness and instruct apart from God.
passages.fullText: 1. See lest any man lead you astray from this way of righteousness, for he teacheth thee apart from God.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: For if thou art able to bear the whole yoke of the Lord, thou shalt be perfect;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Bearing the complete yoke of Christ's commandments leads the Christian soul to evangelical perfection.
passages.fullText: 2. For if thou art able to bear the whole yoke of the Lord, thou shalt be perfect;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: but if thou art not able, do that which thou art able.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Pastoral wisdom urges the faithful to humbly do what they are capable of when full ascetical perfection is beyond their present reach.
passages.fullText: 3. but if thou art not able, do that which thou art able.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But concerning eating, bear that which thou art able;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Disciples are advised to practice dietary self-denial and fasting according to their individual capacity.
passages.fullText: 4. But concerning eating, bear that which thou art able;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: yet abstain by all means from meat sacrificed to idols;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians are strictly commanded to abstain from food sacrificed to idols to preserve fidelity to the true God.
passages.fullText: 5. yet abstain by all means from meat sacrificed to idols;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for it is the worship of dead gods.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Partaking of idolatrous sacrifices is condemned because it constitutes the worship of lifeless, false deities.
passages.fullText: 6. for it is the worship of dead gods.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But concerning baptism, thus shall ye baptize.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache introduces the liturgical and ritual instructions for the valid administration of Holy Baptism.
passages.fullText: 1. But concerning baptism, thus shall ye baptize.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Having first recited all these things, baptize in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit in living (running) water.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Baptism is administered in running water using the essential Trinitarian formula following moral and catechetical instruction.
passages.fullText: 2. Having first recited all these things, baptize in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit in living (running) water.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But if thou hast not living water, then baptize in other water;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Church provides liturgical accommodation allowing baptism in standing water if running water is unavailable.
passages.fullText: 3. But if thou hast not living water, then baptize in other water;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: and if thou art not able in cold, then in warm.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Warm water is permitted for the administration of Baptism when cold water cannot be used.
passages.fullText: 4. and if thou art not able in cold, then in warm.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But if thou hast neither, then pour water on the head thrice in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Baptism by affusion is explicitly validated through the threefold pouring of water upon the head in the Trinitarian name.
passages.fullText: 5. But if thou hast neither, then pour water on the head thrice in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But before the baptism let him that baptizeth and him that is baptized fast, and any others also who are able;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: A preparatory fast is enjoined upon the minister, the catechumen, and the community prior to the celebration of Baptism.
passages.fullText: 6. But before the baptism let him that baptizeth and him that is baptized fast, and any others also who are able;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: and thou shalt order him that is baptized to fast a day or two before.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache prescribes preparatory fasting for catechumens prior to receiving the Sacrament of Baptism.
passages.fullText: 7. and thou shalt order him that is baptized to fast a day or two before.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And let not your fastings be with the hypocrites, for they fast on the second and the fifth day of the week;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians are instructed to distinguish their ascetical practices from the ostentatious fasting of hypocrites.
passages.fullText: 1. And let not your fastings be with the hypocrites, for they fast on the second and the fifth day of the week;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: but do ye keep your fast on the fourth and on the preparation (the sixth) day.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The early Church establishes weekly fasts on Wednesdays and Fridays in solemn remembrance of the Lord's betrayal and Passion.
passages.fullText: 2. but do ye keep your fast on the fourth and on the preparation (the sixth) day.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Neither pray ye as the hypocrites, but as the Lord commanded in His Gospel, thus pray ye:
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Believers are commanded to shun hypocritical prayer and instead pray according to the authentic pattern instituted by Christ in the Gospel.
passages.fullText: 3. Neither pray ye as the hypocrites, but as the Lord commanded in His Gospel, thus pray ye:

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Our Father, which art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Lord's Prayer opens with filial adoration of God the Father and the sanctification of His holy Name.
passages.fullText: 4. Our Father, which art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thy kingdom come;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The faithful petition for the coming of God's Kingdom in hearts, in the Church, and in eschatological fullness.
passages.fullText: 5. Thy kingdom come;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thy will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: This petition expresses total surrender and desire for earthly obedience to correspond perfectly to the divine will in heaven.
passages.fullText: 6. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: give us this day our daily bread;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The soul petitions God for daily sustenance, acknowledging Divine Providence and anticipating the supersubstantial Bread of the Eucharist.
passages.fullText: 7. give us this day our daily bread;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: and forgive us our debt, as we also forgive our debtors;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Divine mercy and forgiveness are asked in direct proportion to the believer's readiness to forgive those who have offended them.
passages.fullText: 8. and forgive us our debt, as we also forgive our debtors;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Christian prays for divine preservation against spiritual temptation and deliverance from Satan's snares.
passages.fullText: 9. and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for Thine is the power and the glory for ever and ever.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The prayer concludes with an ancient liturgical doxology praising the eternal sovereignty, power, and glory of God.
passages.fullText: 10. for Thine is the power and the glory for ever and ever.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Three times in the day pray ye so.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache establishes the regular rule of reciting the Lord's Prayer three times daily as a sanctification of the day.
passages.fullText: 11. Three times in the day pray ye so.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But as touching the eucharistic thanksgiving give ye thanks thus.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache introduces liturgical formulas and instructions for offering the Eucharistic thanksgiving.
passages.fullText: 1. But as touching the eucharistic thanksgiving give ye thanks thus.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: First, as regards the cup:
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The liturgical order of the Eucharistic prayer commences with the thanksgiving over the chalice.
passages.fullText: 2. First, as regards the cup:

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: We give Thee thanks, O our Father, for the holy vine of Thy son David, which Thou madest known unto us through Thy Son Jesus;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Eucharistic prayer over the chalice thanks the Father for the Davidic holy vine revealed through His Son Jesus Christ.
passages.fullText: 3. We give Thee thanks, O our Father, for the holy vine of Thy son David, which Thou madest known unto us through Thy Son Jesus;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thine is the glory for ever and ever.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Eucharistic prayer renders eternal praise and glory unto God the Father.
passages.fullText: 4. Thine is the glory for ever and ever.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Then as regards the broken bread:
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache directs the liturgical thanksgiving to proceed to the blessing of the broken bread.
passages.fullText: 5. Then as regards the broken bread:

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: We give Thee thanks, O our Father, for the life and knowledge which Thou didst make known unto us through Thy Son Jesus;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Eucharistic blessing over the bread gives thanks to the Father for the divine life and knowledge revealed through Christ.
passages.fullText: 6. We give Thee thanks, O our Father, for the life and knowledge which Thou didst make known unto us through Thy Son Jesus;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thine is the glory for ever and ever.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: A liturgical doxology confirms the eternal honor and glory due to the Almighty Father.
passages.fullText: 7. Thine is the glory for ever and ever.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: As this broken bread was scattered upon the mountains and being gathered together became one, so may Thy Church be gathered together from the ends of the earth into Thy kingdom;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The unification of scattered wheat into one Eucharistic bread serves as a typology and prayer for the unity of the Catholic Church gathered from the ends of the earth into God's Kingdom.
passages.fullText: 8. As this broken bread was scattered upon the mountains and being gathered together became one, so may Thy Church be gathered together from the ends of the earth into Thy kingdom;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for Thine is the glory and the power through Jesus Christ for ever and ever.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Eucharistic prayer concludes with a solemn doxology acknowledging the Father's eternal glory and power through Jesus Christ.
passages.fullText: 9. for Thine is the glory and the power through Jesus Christ for ever and ever.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But let no one eat or drink of this eucharistic thanksgiving, but they that have been baptized into the name of the Lord;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Holy Communion is strictly restricted to those who have been incorporated into Christ through Holy Baptism.
passages.fullText: 10. But let no one eat or drink of this eucharistic thanksgiving, but they that have been baptized into the name of the Lord;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: for concerning this also the Lord hath said:
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache grounds its Eucharistic discipline in the authoritative spoken words of the Lord Jesus.
passages.fullText: 11. for concerning this also the Lord hath said:

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Give not that which is holy to the dogs.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Gospel precept against casting holy things to dogs is applied to guard the sacred mysteries of the Holy Eucharist from profanation.
passages.fullText: 12. Give not that which is holy to the dogs.
